section_summary: This section documents U.S. and Allied procedures for controlling civilian entry into occupied Japan, particularly through SCAP Circular No. 8 and the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s Military Permit Secretariat. Cases concern missionaries, businessmen, researchers, returning residents, diplomats’ dependents, shipping personnel, and Japanese repatriates, with repeated attention to diplomatic channels, language qualifications, baggage allowances, and consular visas. The largest recurring case involves clearance of six Irish missionary sisters and authorization for each to carry one ton of baggage.

subfiles.title: Irish Legation note transmitting six nuns’ applications
subfiles.about: Requests airmail transmission to Father Bitter of material concerning six Irish nuns seeking entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Irish Minister asks the Department to forward the enclosed communication to Father Bitter in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Reply returning the Irish nuns’ applications
subfiles.about: Explains why six enclosed applications are being returned to the Irish Legation.
subfiles.summary: The Department notes that Sister St. Enda was cleared but further language information was required for five nuns. It will forward the applications’ new information to the Military Permit Secretariat and returns the originals.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning six Irish sisters
subfiles.about: Records consultations over applications and Japanese-language qualifications for six Irish missionary sisters.
subfiles.summary: State and Joint Chiefs officers agreed that the applications supplied the requested occupational information and should be sent to the Military Permit Secretariat. A later Irish cable reported that the five uncleared nuns had acquired elementary Japanese.

subfiles.title: Syrian acknowledgment of Japan travel regulations
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt and forwarding of the Department’s circular on travel into and from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Syria forwarded the January 17 travel circular and enclosure to its government.

subfiles.title: Clearance and language inquiry for six Irish sisters
subfiles.from: John R. Millett, Military Permit Secretary
subfiles.about: Reports Sister St. Enda’s clearance and requests language information for the remaining Irish sisters.
subfiles.summary: Theater clearance was granted to Angela Fitzgerald; decisions on five others awaited assurances about spoken Japanese or duties not requiring it.

subfiles.title: Language information for five Irish nuns
subfiles.about: Supplies occupational and language information needed to decide five Irish nuns’ applications.
subfiles.summary: The five nuns were teachers whose duties did not require Japanese and had acquired elementary knowledge of the language.

subfiles.title: Approval of the application form for aliens entering Japan
subfiles.about: Records approval and amendment of the standard application form for aliens seeking entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reviewers substituted “nationality” for “citizenship” and required missionaries to specify work relevant to Japanese-language needs.

subfiles.title: Circular note transmitting SCAP Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Explains revised procedures for submitting applications to enter or leave Japan.
subfiles.summary: Governments represented in Japan were to apply through their Tokyo representatives. The State Department would transmit applications for governments without representation there, regardless of existing representation arrangements.

subfiles.title: Conducted tours for in-transit ship passengers
subfiles.about: Announces arrangements for commercial-vessel passengers to tour the Tokyo–Yokohama area.
subfiles.summary: In-transit passengers could take conducted tours and buy souvenirs without military permits.

subfiles.title: Military-permit exemption for Japanese repatriates and deportees
subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese repatriates and deportees no longer need military permits to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Immigration authorities are asked to include passenger numbers and departure ports in normal sailing notices.

subfiles.title: Irish Legation informed of St. Enda’s clearance
subfiles.about: Reports clearance for Sister St. Enda and requests language information on five other Irish sisters.
subfiles.summary: The Department quotes the Military Permit Secretary’s decision and asks whether the remaining sisters know spoken Japanese or hold posts for which it is unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Inquiry regarding Host and Tunold travel applications
subfiles.about: Seeks help advancing travel applications for Th. Host and B. B. Tunold.
subfiles.summary: Moller asks about Host’s Japan permit and requests assistance with Tunold’s Shanghai visa application.

subfiles.title: Request for advice on Cornelius Osgood’s Korea trip
subfiles.about: Requests advice on Yale’s proposal to send Cornelius Osgood to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Acheson asks Far Eastern Affairs for a memorandum assessing Yale’s request.

subfiles.title: Advice on Osgood’s proposed entry into Korea
subfiles.about: Explains current restrictions and recommended passport procedure for Cornelius Osgood.
subfiles.summary: Civilian entry was severely limited, but Osgood could submit a detailed passport application for referral to the War Department and theater commander.

subfiles.title: Yale request supporting Cornelius Osgood
subfiles.about: Requests advice and personal assistance for Cornelius Osgood’s proposed anthropological work in Korea.
subfiles.summary: Furniss endorses Osgood’s experience and asks which authorities should approve his trip.

subfiles.title: Osgood proposal for cultural research in Korea
subfiles.about: Proposes Yale-sponsored cultural research in U.S.-occupied Korea during 1947.
subfiles.summary: Osgood seeks State and War Department approval, transportation, occupation-government cooperation, and permission for side trips to Nanjing or Beijing. His projected research would emphasize indigenous technology and economic implications.

subfiles.title: Biographical data for Cornelius Osgood’s Far East application
subfiles.about: Summarizes Osgood’s education, employment, languages, publications, and field experience.
subfiles.summary: The résumé supports Osgood’s application to undertake Far Eastern research in 1947.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Host and Tunold
subfiles.about: Explains the appropriate channels for Host’s and Tunold’s travel applications.
subfiles.summary: Host should work through Danish representatives, while Tunold should remain in contact with the American Consulate General at Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Reply to Yale concerning Osgood’s Korea trip
subfiles.about: Advises Yale on the procedure for seeking permission for Cornelius Osgood to enter Korea.
subfiles.summary: Osgood should file a detailed passport application, which State would refer to the War Department and theater commander.

subfiles.title: Unauthorized arrival of Charles George Bergin
subfiles.to: Joint Chiefs of Staff and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports Bergin’s arrival in Japan without known prior military clearance.
subfiles.summary: His visit was legitimate, but Manila should be reminded of Joint Chiefs military-permit procedures if it authorized him.

subfiles.title: Travel of Pieter Willem Roman Hesselman
subfiles.about: Reports Hesselman’s selection as assistant trade adviser to a Netherlands military mission.
subfiles.summary: The heavily damaged telegram concerns Hesselman’s proposed official employment and travel.

subfiles.title: Instructions on a White Russian family’s Japan application
subfiles.about: Directs a stateless White Russian applicant to proceed through the French representative in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: French authorities should ask their Tokyo representative to approach SCAP about the family’s entry.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning a White Russian family
subfiles.about: Asks how a stateless White Russian, his Japanese wife, and daughter should seek permanent residence in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hanoi requests instructions on the correct visa procedure for the family.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for despatch 3626
subfiles.about: Designates a copy of despatch 3626 as the official record copy.
subfiles.summary: Record-copy form replacing an unreturned original action copy.

subfiles.title: Panamanian visa request for James G. Embry
subfiles.about: Transmits Panama’s request that the U.S. representative at Yokohama issue Embry an immigrant visa.
subfiles.summary: Panama seeks a visa for American citizen James G. Embry at his wife’s request.

subfiles.title: Panamanian Foreign Ministry note concerning Embry
subfiles.about: Requests U.S. consular assistance in issuing James G. Embry a Panamanian immigrant visa.
subfiles.summary: The visa would be issued after Embry presented health and conduct certificates.

subfiles.title: Action copy of despatch 3626
subfiles.about: Duplicates the embassy despatch forwarding Panama’s visa request for James G. Embry.
subfiles.summary: Action copy of the March 19 despatch concerning Embry’s Panamanian visa.

subfiles.title: Central Translating Division receipt for TC 37014
subfiles.about: Records receipt and return of translation control item 37014.
subfiles.summary: Translation-control cover sheet for the Panamanian note.

subfiles.title: Translation of Panamanian note 696
subfiles.about: Provides an English translation of Panama’s request for an immigrant visa for James G. Embry.
subfiles.summary: Panama asks the U.S. consul at Yokohama to visa Embry’s passport after health and conduct checks.

subfiles.title: Additional Spanish copy of Panamanian note 696
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Spanish Foreign Ministry request concerning James G. Embry.
subfiles.summary: Spanish copy of Panama’s immigrant-visa request for Embry.

subfiles.title: Verification of James G. Embry’s naval status
subfiles.about: Records inquiries into Embry’s citizenship, naval service, and ship’s expected arrival.
subfiles.summary: Navy records placed Ensign Embry aboard USS Kankakee, due at Yokosuka on April 29.

subfiles.title: Instruction to issue Embry’s Panamanian visa
subfiles.about: Authorizes compliance with Panama’s visa request if the Yokohama office perceives no objection.
subfiles.summary: Despite finding no passport record, State asks Yokohama to assist Embry if circumstances permit.

subfiles.title: Illegible filing or routing slip
subfiles.about: Contains only fragmentary, illegible routing notations.
subfiles.summary: Illegible administrative slip.

subfiles.title: Malcolm Duncan request to re-enter Japan
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Duncan, his Japanese wife, and child to return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Duncan describes his former residence and teaching in Japan, wartime British naval service, and postwar losses. He hopes to travel from Hong Kong through Kure in June or July.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Malcolm Duncan’s request
subfiles.about: Duplicates Duncan’s request for permission to return to Japan with his family.
subfiles.summary: Duncan recounts his residence, naval service, financial losses, and proposed June or July return via Hong Kong and Kure.

subfiles.title: Instruction concerning Malcolm Duncan
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Bangkok
subfiles.about: Directs Bangkok to explain the proper British diplomatic channel for Duncan’s application.
subfiles.summary: Duncan should approach the British representative in Bangkok or the British Foreign Office under SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for telegram or airgram
subfiles.about: Designates a white copy to replace an unreturned action copy.
subfiles.summary: Administrative record-copy replacement form.

subfiles.title: Salvage mission request for Charles English Henderson
subfiles.about: Requests urgent entry clearance for Henderson to conduct salvage work in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Henderson sought a three-month trip to arrange salvage of SS Lake Sapor and its cargo.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning clearance and baggage for six Irish sisters
subfiles.about: Records inquiries about reported clearance and baggage allowances for six Irish missionary sisters.
subfiles.summary: The Irish Legation reported unofficial word of approval and asked whether each nun could carry one ton of baggage. The Military Permit Secretariat agreed to cable Tokyo for confirmation and a baggage ruling.

subfiles.title: Travel clearance for Horne and Segurola
subfiles.about: States that the military has no objection to Horne and Segurola traveling to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Military travel clearance is granted to Mercedes Horne and Ana Segurola.

subfiles.title: Travel clearance for Rouben Lionel Grover Challis
subfiles.about: States that the military has no objection to Challis traveling to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Rouben Lionel Grover Challis is cleared for travel to Japan.

subfiles.title: File search for Levi, Goldman, and Menache Cousins
subfiles.about: Records unsuccessful file checks for Ralph Levi, Isaac Goldman, and Menache Cousins.
subfiles.summary: Two State Department offices reported no information on the named individuals or firm.

subfiles.title: Clearance for Spanish diplomatic dependents
subfiles.about: Reports entry clearance for the wife and children of a new Spanish diplomatic representative.
subfiles.summary: SCAP cleared Yvonne de Ojeda and three children and renewed Mr. Ojeda’s clearance.

subfiles.title: Reply on Soviet treatment of American personnel
subfiles.about: Identifies War Department records as the best source on Soviet restrictions affecting Americans.
subfiles.summary: Allied Control Commission reports in War Department files were said to document movement, customs, and entry restrictions in Eastern Europe.

subfiles.title: European Affairs response on Soviet travel restrictions
subfiles.about: Recommends consulting Allied Control Commission reports concerning restrictions on Americans.
subfiles.summary: Relevant reports were held by the War Department’s Plans and Operations Division, which would prepare a resulting report.

subfiles.title: Request to European Affairs for information
subfiles.about: Seeks information on Soviet treatment of Americans to guide SCAP policy toward Soviet personnel.
subfiles.summary: Anderson requests facts or reply suggestions concerning movement, customs, and entry and exit requirements.

subfiles.title: War Department request on Soviet restrictions
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.about: Requests information comparing Soviet controls on Americans for use by CINCFE and SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The War Department seeks details from Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, and other Soviet satellite areas.

subfiles.title: Copy of request to European Affairs
subfiles.about: Copies the request for guidance on Soviet restrictions and their relevance to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: True copy of Anderson’s memorandum seeking information on Soviet controls.

subfiles.title: Copy of War Department information request
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.about: Duplicates the War Department request for information on Soviet treatment of Americans.
subfiles.summary: Copy requests comparative data for policy on Soviet mission personnel in Japan.

subfiles.title: Conference on administration of SCAP Circular No. 8
subfiles.about: Records agreement on handling foreign-government applications under SCAP Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: Officials debated unequal treatment of American and foreign business applications. They agreed not to seek revision of Circular No. 8 and to transmit foreign governmental requests according to established representation practice while informing interested divisions.

subfiles.title: Information sheets for Japanese voluntary repatriates
subfiles.about: Proposes standardized baggage, funds, and vaccination guidance for Japanese repatriates.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg recommends mimeographing at least 500 information sets and warns that export and baggage rules may change.

subfiles.title: Turkish textile buyers’ proposed mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Requests expedited travel for three Turkish representatives connected with a major textile contract.
subfiles.summary: SCAP reportedly accepted the mission of Cevdet Aydinelli, Ragip Sipahi, and Ismail Kavadar to Japan.

subfiles.title: Routing note on five Irish sisters’ clearances
subfiles.about: Forwards a Joint Chiefs memorandum clearing five Irish sisters for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Brief transmittal of military travel clearances for five nuns.

subfiles.title: Clearance and baggage allowance for Irish sisters
subfiles.about: Clears five Irish sisters and grants baggage allowances to all six.
subfiles.summary: Five sisters are cleared, and each—including previously cleared Angela Fitzgerald—may take one ton of baggage.

subfiles.title: Interpretation of the Irish sisters’ baggage allowance
subfiles.about: Clarifies that the one-ton allowance applies separately to each Irish sister.
subfiles.summary: The Military Permit Secretariat confirmed that every nun could bring one ton of baggage.

subfiles.title: B. E. Ancona business-travel application
subfiles.about: Reports Ancona’s application for a three-month textile-buying trip to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The embassy describes his firm’s resources but notes concerns about director Selim Sassoon’s local business relationships.

subfiles.title: Clearances for Horne, Segurola, and Gorini
subfiles.about: Reviews efforts to secure Japan entry clearances for two Spanish and one Italian nun.
subfiles.summary: The Spanish nuns were cleared through Spanish channels, while SCAP also approved Italian Mother Gorini. Because the Italian reply was delayed and clearances expired after sixty days, State agreed to notify the Italian Embassy of the Joint Chiefs’ information.

subfiles.title: Baghdad despatch transmitting the Moche application
subfiles.about: Transmits Victor Moche’s application for permission for himself and his wife to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The embassy asks for SCAP’s decision because Iraq has no representation in Japan.

subfiles.title: Victor Chouah Moche application to return to Kobe
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests entry permits for Moche and his wife to resume residence in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Moche describes his prewar business, property left in Japan, depleted funds, Iraqi passport, and proposed route through Bangkok and Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Moche travel application
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Duplicates Moche’s request to return to Kobe with his wife.
subfiles.summary: Copy details Moche’s former residence, business interests, passport, and proposed travel route.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Victor Moche’s application
subfiles.about: Certifies Moche’s voluntary execution of the attached application.
subfiles.summary: The American Vice Consul at Baghdad notarizes Moche’s signature.

subfiles.title: Referral of the Moche application to the Military Permit Secretary
subfiles.about: Requests a decision on whether Victor Moche and his wife may proceed to Japan.
subfiles.summary: State encloses the Iraqi national’s application received through the Baghdad embassy.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Baghdad concerning Moche’s application
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Baghdad
subfiles.about: Explains the procedural defect in Moche’s application while confirming its referral to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Although the application should have come through the Iraqi Government, State forwards it and promises to report the decision.

subfiles.title: Irish Legation notified of final clearances and baggage
subfiles.about: Confirms clearance of all six Irish nuns and explains their documentation and baggage allowances.
subfiles.summary: SCAP cleared the remaining five sisters, joining Sister St. Enda, and authorized one ton of baggage for each. The note encloses Circular No. 8 and reminds the Legation that every traveler must carry an English clearance statement containing the prescribed information.

subfiles.title: India Welfare League appeal for Haji Moosa Ismail
subfiles.about: Requests assistance obtaining permission for a Bombay merchant to visit Japan and China.
subfiles.summary: Khan supports Haji Moosa Ismail’s proposed business journey and asks to discuss the case during a Washington visit.

subfiles.title: Ralph S. Levi business-travel application
subfiles.about: Reports Levi’s application for a twelve-month purchasing trip to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Levi planned to buy textiles, porcelain, ginger, and raw silk while importing manufacturing materials; the embassy endorsed his firm.

subfiles.title: Reply on Ancona and Levi applications
subfiles.about: Directs Ancona and Levi to seek SCAP approval through their national representatives in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Their Italian and British representatives must present the applications; private business trips were not yet generally approved.

subfiles.title: Document charge-out card
subfiles.about: Blank form for recording the charging and return of a document.
subfiles.summary: Blank document charge-out card.
